purpose: Inventory existing packet<->chunk lineage reports/scripts, tag each finding with its actual population definition and proof level, and designate the current canonical resolver owner (if any exists). Does not attempt a new join or resolver.
explicitRule: Numbers below MUST NOT be compared across rows as if they describe the same population. Each entry carries its own population definition.

inventory.population: all atlas_packets (61,660) vs all codebase_chunk_index rows as they existed at that time (55,206)
inventory.method: Tries every plausible direct field-join at once (source_ref, packet_key, feature_id, tree_node_id, qdrant_id), no hash comparison.
inventory.proofLevel: NONE -- every direct-field join except source_ref (which fans out) resolves to zero pairs. treeNodeId here is a literal FK-value join attempt (not the atlas_ast_nodes bridge speculated in PACKET-CHUNK-RESOLVE-01A) and it also returns 0 -- independent evidence against tree_node_id as a direct resolver.

inventory.population: 111 rows bound to a specific current workspace revision (sha256:55edaaad...) -- the narrowest, most current-revision-strict population of any report in this inventory
inventory.method: Checks whether codebase_chunk_index.content_hash (explicitly confirmed per-chunk digest, NOT a whole-source digest) agrees with a proven current-workspace Graphify binding hash for the same source.
inventory.hashGrainFinding: codebaseChunkIndexContentHash is a per-chunk digest, not equal to a whole-source digest for multi-chunk files -- this is the load-bearing fact that makes source_ref-group-level hash agreement (see graphify-packet-lineage-census-v1 below) an unsafe proxy for row-level identity.
inventory.proofLevel: STRICTEST CHECK IN THIS INVENTORY -- current-workspace-revision-bound, respects per-chunk hash grain. Result: zero exact resolutions.

inventory.population: full 61,660-row atlas_packets corpus, cross-referenced against atlas_artifacts (58,312 rows) and codebase_chunk_index (55,853 rows) as independent hash authorities -- not a join, a coverage/availability survey
inventory.method: Surveys which hash-bearing columns exist and how populated they are; does not attempt to prove hash-domain equivalence between them.
inventory.keyLead: atlas_artifacts.content_hash is 99.99% populated -- by far the richest hash surface found anywhere in this inventory, on either side of the investigation.
inventory.proofLevel: NONE -- own stated conclusion is REVIEW_REQUIRED: hash equivalence between atlas_artifacts.content_hash and codebase_chunk_index.content_hash is asserted as an open question, not proven. chunk_artifact_hash_agreements: 0 is itself evidence the two hash domains may not currently agree at all (though this could also mean they were never compared correctly -- domain compatibility, not just raw comparison, must be established first).

inventory.population: full 61,660-row atlas_packets corpus, joined to codebase_chunk_index GROUPED BY source_ref (not joined row-to-row)
inventory.method: For each source_ref, computes count(DISTINCT lower(content_hash)) across all codebase_chunk_index rows sharing that source_ref. Only accepts a source as an 'exact' candidate when that count is exactly 1 (i.e. every chunk row for that file happens to share one hash value) AND the packet's own content_hash equals it. Explicitly refuses to pick a winner when the group has >1 distinct hash (classified ambiguous) -- this correctly avoids the earlier BRIDGE-RECON-DRY-02 fan-out bug at the GROUP level.
inventory.criticalCaveat: This 'exact: 332' and gates.packetContentIntegrity.proven=true DO NOT mean 332 rows have a proven single canonical codebase_chunk_index.id. The check is group-hash-agreement, not row identity: (a) it never selects one specific chunk row even for the 'exact' 332 (only proves the packet's hash matches whatever single hash value the whole source_ref group shares); (b) per the current-workspace-packet-chunk-join-v1 finding above, chunk-level content_hash is a per-chunk digest, so a source_ref group having only 1 distinct hash across possibly-many rows more likely means those rows are duplicate/stale re-indexations of an unchanged file, not proof of freshness; (c) it applies no workspace/revision-currency check at all, unlike current-workspace-packet-chunk-join-v1 (which DID apply that check on a stricter 111-row population and got zero). The internal 'proven: true' flag in this report's own gates block should be read as 'group-hash-agreement proven', not 'canonical packet-chunk identity proven' -- the report's naming is misleading relative to what it actually establishes.
inventory.proofLevel: GROUP-LEVEL HASH AGREEMENT ONLY, NOT ROW IDENTITY, NOT REVISION-QUALIFIED

convergentFinding: Four independent scripts, four different methods, overlapping-but-not-identical populations, all reach the same underlying conclusion once population and proof-level are accounted for: there is currently no populated field or join path in this Postgres corpus that resolves a packet to exactly one canonical, revision-qualified codebase_chunk_index row. The strictest check (current-workspace-packet-chunk-join-v1, current-workspace-revision-bound, per-chunk hash grain) found zero. The loosest check (graphify-packet-lineage-census-v1's 332) only proves group-level hash agreement, not row identity, and does not survive the stricter check's own more rigorous method being applied to a subset of the same underlying question. This session's own PACKET-CHUNK-RESOLVE-01A (chunk_id: 0/1390) and the 2026-08-28 packet-chunk-mapping-audit (packetKey/featureId/treeNodeId: 0 pairs each) both independently corroborate the same negative result via yet other fields.
designatedCanonicalOwner: NONE EXISTS YET. No script in this inventory is a validated, revision-qualified, single-row packet->chunk resolver. The closest unexploited lead is atlas_artifacts.content_hash (99.99% populated, unlike every atlas_packets-local field checked in this session or prior ones) -- but its own author explicitly flagged hash-domain equivalence to codebase_chunk_index.content_hash as REVIEW_REQUIRED, unproven. This is exactly the WORKSTATION-HASH-DOMAIN-01 gate that must run before any cardinality/join work reuses this surface.
recommendedNextGate: WORKSTATION-HASH-DOMAIN-01 -- read-only. Find and read the actual producer code for atlas_artifacts.content_hash and codebase_chunk_index.content_hash (algorithm, encoding, normalization, source-byte-range vs whole-file, truncation, revision binding) and determine whether the two hash domains are even comparable before running any cardinality check against them. Do not proceed to a join/cardinality gate until this is proven either way.

atlas_artifacts_content_hash.contentDomain: entry.content is an ArtifactLogEntry.content field, typed against artifact_type: 'summary' | 'embedding' | 'latent64' | 'som_cell' | 'redis_cache' | 'markdown' | 'qdrant_payload' | 'gemma4_prompt' | 'gemma4_output' | 'feature_labels' | 'gan_report' | 'benchmark' | 'trace'. This is a dedup hash over GENERATED artifact output content (a summary string, a serialized embedding, etc.) -- never over source code chunk bytes.
atlas_artifacts_content_hash.purpose: Deduplication key so logArtifact() can detect 'this exact artifact was already generated' before inserting a new atlas_artifacts row -- not an identity bridge to source content.

codebase_chunk_index_content_hash.contentDomain: Per already-read current-workspace-packet-chunk-join-v1.json: 'per-chunk digest; not equal to a whole-source digest for multi-chunk files' -- i.e. a digest of actual source chunk bytes.
codebase_chunk_index_content_hash.producerNotFullyTraced: Exact writer script not pinned down in this pass (grep for INSERT/UPDATE codebase_chunk_index + createHash across scripts/ did not surface one obvious canonical writer among the candidates checked; time-boxed, not exhaustively chased since the domain-incompatibility finding below already closes the gate regardless of the exact producer).

workstationHashDomain01.verdict: atlas_artifacts.content_hash and codebase_chunk_index.content_hash hash two structurally different content domains (generated-artifact output vs. source-chunk bytes) by construction, not merely by unproven-in-practice coincidence. A SHA-256 of a Gemma4 summary and a SHA-256 of the source code it summarizes have no reason to ever match except by accident. This is fully consistent with -- not contradicted by -- the already-recorded empirical finding chunk_artifact_hash_agreements: 0 in atlas-packet-content-hash-lineage-v1.json: that 0 is the expected result of comparing hashes of unrelated content, not evidence of a data gap.
workstationHashDomain01.conclusion: atlas_artifacts.content_hash, despite being 99.99% populated, is CLOSED as a non-viable packet->chunk resolver. It is not a hash-domain-compatibility question that further proof could resolve -- the domains are definitionally different. This was the single most promising unexploited lead in the inventory; its closure means every candidate surfaced across all four inventoried reports, this session's own PACKET-CHUNK-RESOLVE-01A, and the 2026-08-28 packet-chunk-mapping-audit is now exhausted.

epistemicCorrection: The conclusion is NOT 'packet->chunk identity does not exist'. It is 'packet->chunk identity cannot be derived exactly from the currently inventoried and populated historical evidence'. An evidence limitation is not an ontological statement -- a future authoritative source (e.g. a historical revision checkout, or a producer log never yet inventoried) could still recover some of these. Historical rows are therefore classified UNRESOLVED_WITH_CURRENT_EVIDENCE, not permanently unresolved.
decision: OPTION_A_SELECTED: capture canonical chunk identity at packet-creation time going forward. No synthetic/approximate backfill of historical rows. Option B (approximate historical realignment) is retained as a separate, explicitly non-canonical, optional future experiment -- see historicalRealignmentExperiment below -- never as a substitute for real lineage capture.

historicalRealignmentExperiment.name: HISTORICAL-LINEAGE-REALIGNMENT-EXP-01
historicalRealignmentExperiment.scope: source reconstruction via historical revision checkout where available, deterministic re-chunk, content-span/AST alignment, candidate match confidence, evidence receipt

Only exact reconstruction against authoritative historical source bytes+revision could graduate a row out of UNRESOLVED_WITH_CURRENT_EVIDENCE, and that graduation is a separate, later, explicitly-gated decision -- not automatic from this experiment's output.

canonicalContract.hardRule: The packet writer MUST receive these values from an upstream canonical chunk object at creation time. It must NEVER reconstruct them after the fact from source paths, hashes, AST coordinates, Qdrant payloads, or nearest-match heuristics.
canonicalContract.downstreamConsumerContract: CanonicalPacketChunkResolutionV1 -- { status: 'EXACT', packetKey, canonicalChunkId, sourceRef, sourceRevision, evidenceRefs[], resolverRevision } | { status: 'AMBIGUOUS'|'REVISION_UNPROVEN'|'SOURCE_NAMESPACE_UNPROVEN'|'MISSING', packetKey, evidenceRefs[], resolverRevision }. ProjectionRegistryV1 / BRIDGE-RECON-DRY-03 / RECON-CANARY-01 may consume EXACT rows only, and must never infer packet<->chunk identity themselves.

packetChunkLineageWriter01.method: grep for all scripts that both reference codebase_chunk_index AND write INSERT INTO atlas_packets, then read each candidate's actual query/insert logic.

activeProducer.selfDocumented: '40K+ chunks were indexed in Qdrant before being registered to atlas_packets. These orphans have no packet_key, directory_path, or feature_id in Postgres.' -- this IS the documented root cause of the entire lineage gap chased across all prior gates.
activeProducer.orphanQuery: SELECT DISTINCT cci.relative_path as source_ref FROM codebase_chunk_index cci WHERE ... NOT IN (SELECT source_ref FROM atlas_packets ...) -- never selects cci.id or cci.chunk_id
activeProducer.packetKeyDerivation: 'packet:' + sha256(sourceRef).slice(0,12) -- hashed from the file path STRING, not chunk content or a chunk row identity
activeProducer.rootCauseConfirmed: The DISTINCT ON relative_path in the orphan-discovery query is the structural origin of the source_ref fan-out found in every downstream investigation (BRIDGE-RECON-DRY-02, packet-chunk-mapping-audit, this session's own census) -- it deliberately collapses N codebase_chunk_index rows into 1 atlas_packets row by construction, at the moment of packet creation, not as a later join artifact.

deadDangerousCandidate.liveCallers: NONE found outside its own canonical-id-hierarchy.spec.ts -- confirmed dead code, not currently wired into any packet-creation path.
deadDangerousCandidate.whyDangerous: Presents a fully-typed CanonicalIDHierarchy contract that superficially looks like exactly the canonical PacketChunkLineageV1 contract this investigation is trying to build -- but repository_id, directory_id, file_id, module_id, symbol_id, AND chunk_id are ALL set via randomUUID(), never read from a real row. A future agent could easily mistake this for 'the contract already exists, just wire it in' and would be wiring in synthetic identity fabrication, exactly what PACKET-CHUNK-LINEAGE-CONTRACT-01's hard rule ('must NEVER reconstruct after the fact ... or nearest-match heuristics') exists to prevent.

deadDangerousCandidate.disposition: Leave as dead code for now (out of scope for this read-only gate); flag for archival or an explicit 'DEAD -- do not wire' marker when PACKET-CHUNK-LINEAGE-CONTRACT-01 is built, so it cannot be mistaken for the real contract.

packetChunkLineageContract01.shape: PacketChunkMembershipV1: packetKey, canonicalChunkId, chunkRowId, sourceRef, sourceNamespace (required, non-empty), sourceRevision (nullable), membershipStatus (EXACT_SINGLE_MEMBER|EXACT_MULTI_MEMBER only -- no ambiguous/candidate statuses admitted into this table), revisionStatus (PROVEN|UNPROVEN), chunkOrdinal, lineageProducerRevision, evidenceRefs[]. .strict() Zod schema with a .refine() enforcing revisionStatus PROVEN iff sourceRevision is non-null.
packetChunkLineageContract01.relationShape: atlas_packet_chunk_lineage. NOT NULL on all fields except source_revision. UNIQUE(packet_key, canonical_chunk_id) ONLY -- see packetChunkLineageMigration01.uniquenessCorrection below for why lineage_producer_revision was deliberately removed from an earlier draft of this key.
packetChunkLineageContract01.notDoneThisGate: No schema-postgres.ts change, no Drizzle migration, no DB writes. PACKET-CHUNK-LINEAGE-MIGRATION-01 (disposable DB first) is a separate, later gate per explicit instruction.
packetChunkLineageContract01.checkpointNote: This is a deliberate semantic checkpoint: the contract is frozen and tested (8/8) while zero PostgreSQL schema/migration work has been done. DB schema writes: 0. Canonical lineage writes: 0. Historical backfill writes: 0. MIGRATION-01 is a separate, later gate -- do not combine physical migration work into this checkpoint.

packetChunkLineageMigration01.method: Proved on a disposable database first (CREATE DATABASE atlas_pcl_migration_disposable in the same Postgres instance, dropped after each round), then applied identically (CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS only) to the live legal_ai_db -- purely additive, no ALTER, zero risk to existing data.

uniquenessCorrection.problem: Including lineage_producer_revision in the uniqueness key would let a second producer re-observing the exact same (packet, chunk) relationship insert a SECOND canonical membership row for it -- inflating downstream vote/cardinality counts (e.g. counting a packet's members would double-count a re-observed membership). Caught before any live data was written under the flawed key -- the first live application (0 rows) was dropped and redone under the corrected key before any real usage.
uniquenessCorrection.corrected: UNIQUE(packet_key, canonical_chunk_id) only. lineage_producer_revision and evidence_refs are provenance ON the one canonical row, not part of membership identity. A producer re-observing an existing membership must UPSERT (ON CONFLICT (packet_key, canonical_chunk_id) DO UPDATE) against the existing row, never insert a new one. Append-only observation history, if ever needed, belongs in a separate execution-evidence table -- never conflated with this canonical membership relation.
uniquenessCorrection.namespaceFkAvoided: source_namespace is plain text, deliberately not a foreign key to atlas_packets.repository_id, which is confirmed corrupted (58,365/58,365 populated values all distinct -- synthetic randomUUID()-per-row).

realBugsFoundAndFixedDuringThisGate.bug: Replay-gate logic bug (not a data problem): expectBeforeCount was hardcoded per-fixture for a truly-first run (0 for new fixtures, 5 for the pre-existing overlap). On the replay pass within the same script execution, pass 1 had already committed real rows for SINGLE/FEW/MANY, so their real beforeMembershipCount on replay was legitimately non-zero -- but the check still compared against the static 0, producing a false ROLLBACK_MISMATCH on 3 of 4 replay fixtures despite every other check (checksum, foreign/missing/duplicate/synthetic counts) being exactly correct.
realBugsFoundAndFixedDuringThisGate.fix: expectBeforeCount is now computed per-pass: proposed.length on the replay pass (an idempotent UPSERT always leaves count == proposed.length), the original static value only on the initial pass. Reset the 3 affected fixture rows and re-ran clean to get an honest initial+replay proof under the fix, rather than trusting the first (partially-correct, partially-buggy) run's output.

openDesignQuestionSurfacedByThisGate_RES: STATUS: RESOLVED_SUPERSEDED. The a/b/c fork below is preserved verbatim for history only -- do not reopen it. The decision was made in the very next exchange (see architecturalCorrection, reinterpretedFanOutBug, revisedCanonicalContract below): none of a/b/c as originally framed. atlas_packets stays FILE-granularity (option (b)'s premise, rejected as knowingly lossy) and chunk lineage is represented as an explicit normalized 1:N relation (closest to (c), but as a relational table -- atlas_packet_chunk_lineage -- never as an array column on atlas_packets). This is now frozen in PacketChunkMembershipV1 (packetChunkLineageContract01 below) and physically implemented in packetChunkLineageMigration01. Original superseded text: atlas_packets is currently FILE-granularity (one row per source_ref, by register-orphaned-chunks.mjs's own DISTINCT design) while codebase_chunk_index is CHUNK-granularity (many rows per source_ref for multi-chunk files). PacketChunkLineageV1's canonicalChunkId as a single string assumes a 1:1 packet-to-chunk relationship that does not match the current packet model. PACKET-CHUNK-LINEAGE-CONTRACT-01 must resolve this explicitly -- e.g. either (a) redefine packet granularity to be chunk-level going forward (breaking change to what a 'packet' means), or (b) keep packets file-level and define canonicalChunkId as 'the primary/representative chunk for this file' under an explicit, documented rule (e.g. lowest line_start), or (c) change canonicalChunkId to canonicalChunkIds: string[] and drop the single-EXACT-resolution assumption entirely. This gate surfaces the question; it does not answer it.
architecturalCorrection: The FILE-vs-chunk fork above was framed incorrectly as a-vs-b-vs-c. The correct model is closest to (c) but normalized as an explicit relational membership, not an array embedded in atlas_packets: packet identity and chunk identity are NOT the same thing -- a packet<->chunk relation is LINEAGE MEMBERSHIP (1 FILE packet contains/was-derived-from N canonical chunks), not identity equality. Do not redefine packets to chunk-granularity (large breaking migration) and do not pick a 'representative chunk' (would knowingly turn a many-chunk file into a false 1:1 identity). Preserve atlas_packets granularity as-is.
reinterpretedFanOutBug: There were two distinct bugs conflated as one. BUG (real, this is what invalidated BRIDGE-RECON-DRY-02): a script picks one arbitrary chunk out of N candidates sharing a source_ref and treats that arbitrary choice as canonical packet identity. NOT A BUG (legitimate, once membership replaces identity-equality as the model): one FILE packet genuinely has N canonical chunk members -- an exact 37-chunk file packet is not ambiguous merely because cardinality is 37, if all 37 chunks are proven members of that exact file/revision. Every downstream gate must stop labeling every multi-chunk match as UNRESOLVED_PACKET_TO_CHUNK_AMBIGUITY on cardinality alone -- membership classification needs its own vocabulary: EXACT_SINGLE_MEMBER, EXACT_MULTI_MEMBER, SOURCE_NAMESPACE_UNPROVEN, SOURCE_REVISION_UNPROVEN, NO_MEMBER, CONFLICTING_MEMBERSHIP.

revisedCanonicalContract.name: PacketChunkMembershipV1 (supersedes the earlier single-canonicalChunkId PacketChunkLineageV1 shape recorded above)

shape.canonicalChunkId: string -- codebase_chunk_index.chunk_id (durable) of ONE member chunk
shape.chunkRowId: string -- codebase_chunk_index.id (uuid PK) of that same member chunk, physical coordinate only

revisedCanonicalContract.persistenceModel: A normalized relation, NOT an array embedded in atlas_packets: atlas_packet_chunk_lineage(packet_key, canonical_chunk_id, chunk_row_id, source_ref, source_namespace, source_revision, chunk_ordinal, lineage_producer_revision, created_at), uniqueness at minimum on (packet_key, canonical_chunk_id, source_revision) pending final revision-identity design. For a 37-chunk file: 1 atlas_packets row + 37 atlas_packet_chunk_lineage rows -- never 37 atlas_packets rows, never 1 arbitrarily-chosen chunk.
revisedCanonicalContract.hardRule: The writer fix for register-orphaned-chunks.mjs must NOT become SELECT cci.chunk_id LIMIT 1 or ORDER BY line_start LIMIT 1. It must preserve the file packet and write one membership row per canonical chunk retained from codebase_chunk_index, group-by canonical source identity, create the FILE packet once.

downstreamProjectionImplication: ProjectionRegistryV1 itself remains valid (it resolves a canonical REPRESENTATION identity, not packet identity). But the upstream flow must stop assuming packet<->one chunk<->one Qdrant point. Correct shape: FILE packet -> PacketChunkMembershipV1 (1:N) -> canonical chunk -> semantic_768 projection -> ProjectionRegistryV1. BRIDGE-RECON-DRY-03 must therefore operate PER MEMBERSHIP, not per packet alone -- for packet 'foo' with chunks A/B/C, the answer is 'chunk A -> projection A, chunk B -> projection B, chunk C -> projection C', never 'which of A/B/C is the real projection for packet foo'.
deadCodeFenceRequirement: canonical-id-hierarchy.ts's generateIDHierarchy() is not to be deleted this gate, but must be marked DEAD -- NON-CANONICAL ID GENERATOR -- DO NOT USE FOR PERSISTED ATLAS IDENTITY when the contract patch lands, plus an architecture check (test or lint rule) ensuring the packet lineage writer never imports it. Governing invariant: persisted canonicalChunkId MUST originate from an existing canonical chunk record (a real codebase_chunk_index row read at write time); it MUST NOT be created via randomUUID(), a hash of source_ref, a nearest-vector match, or an AST-derived fallback. The 6 unexplained atlas_packets.chunk_id values found populated-but-unresolvable in PACKET-CHUNK-RESOLVE-01A are NOT retroactively attributed to canonical-id-hierarchy.ts without individual tracing -- they remain classified ORIGIN_UNPROVEN, not blamed on this dead module without evidence.
